comparisons.peer_summary: The 2024 Restructuring Plan resulted in $2.2 billion in employee severance and benefit charges in 2024, alongside $442 million in non-cash impairments of construction-in-progress assets and $103 million in lease-related impairments.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and INTC disclose significant restructuring charges in fiscal year 2024 that include non-cash asset impairments and employee severance costs. AVGO lists 'fixed asset impairment' and 'employee exit programs' as primary components of its non-recurring charges. Similarly, INTC details a 2024 Restructuring Plan that resulted in $2.2 billion in employee severance and benefit charges, alongside $442 million in non-cash impairments of construction-in-progress assets and $103 million in lease-related impairments. While both companies incurred charges for facility/asset exits and headcount reductions, INTC’s disclosures in 2024 also included massive non-restructuring impairment charges ($3.3B manufacturing, $3.1B goodwill) distinct from its specific restructuring plan, whereas AVGO’s disclosed restructuring scope is more tightly defined around its operational alignment and litigation costs.

sentences.text: Restructuring and other charges consist primarily of non-recurring charges related to compensation costs associated with employee exit programs, IP litigation, alignment of our global manufacturing operations, rationalization of product development program costs, facility and lease abandonments, fixed asset impairment, IPR&D impairment, and other exit costs, including curtailment of service or supply agreements.
Employee severance and benefit arrangements includes net charges relating to the 2024 Restructuring Plan of $2.2 billion in 2024.

Asset impairment charges in 2024 includes non-cash charges associated with the 2024 Restructuring Plan, including $442 million of non-cash impairments of construction-in-progress assets associated with our decision to exit and outsource manufacturing capabilities for certain internal test hardware; and $103 million of non-cash impairments of operating leased assets and related leasehold improvements resulting from real estate consolidations and exits.

comparisons.peer_summary: Fiscal 2023 other expenses consisted of $712 million in restructuring charges (mostly severance from cost reduction actions) and a $150 million intangible asset impairment charge for in-process research and development.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and QCOM both identify employee severance and asset impairments as key components of their restructuring-related charges. AVGO explicitly includes 'compensation costs associated with employee exit programs' and 'IPR&D impairment' in its restructuring charges. QCOM’s fiscal 2023 other expenses included $712 million in restructuring charges (substantially all severance) and a $150 million intangible asset impairment charge related to in-process research and development (IPR&D). Both disclosures highlight the overlap between operational restructuring (severance) and strategic write-downs (IPR&D), although the timing differs (AVGO 2024 vs QCOM 2023 reference in the specific candidate sentence, though QCOM also has a 2024 restructuring candidate qcom_2024_7_D014 which shows a smaller $107M restructuring charge). The similarity lies in the specific inclusion of IPR&D impairments and severance as parts of the broader restructuring charge narrative.

sentences.text: Restructuring and other charges consist primarily of non-recurring charges related to compensation costs associated with employee exit programs, IP litigation, alignment of our global manufacturing operations, rationalization of product development program costs, facility and lease abandonments, fixed asset impairment, IPR&D impairment, and other exit costs, including curtailment of service or supply agreements.

Other expenses in fiscal 2023 consisted of $712 million in total restructuring and restructuring-related charges (substantially all of which related to severance costs, resulting from certain cost reduction actions committed to in fiscal 2023 and a $150 million intangible asset impairment charge related to in-process research and development.
